What Is the Byzantine Rite?
lessons.about: Where Byzantine Catholics come from, how they pray, and how they belong to the one Catholic Church, for kids.

quiz.q: Byzantine worship grew from the way Christians prayed in Antioch.
quiz.why: True! The Catholic Encyclopedia says it “is derived from that of Antioch.”

quiz.q: What do Byzantine Catholics and Roman Catholics share?
quiz.why: We share one faith and the same seven sacraments. We just pray in different ways (CCC 1202).

quiz.q: “It was in ____ that the disciples were first called Christians.”
quiz.why: Acts 11:26. Christians got their name in the city of Antioch.

quiz.q: The Catholic Church is only the Roman, or Latin, Church.
quiz.why: False! The Catholic Church is a family of Churches, Eastern and Western (Christ – Our Pascha 285).

quiz.q: Who are all the Catholic Churches united with?
choices: The Pope, who takes Saint Peter’s place
quiz.why: All the Catholic Churches are united with the Pope, “the successor of the apostle Peter” (Christ – Our Pascha 291).

transcript: Some Catholics pray with icons and receive communion with a spoon, but why do they do this, and who are they? Well, let’s get a quick introduction to Byzantine Rite Catholics with this lesson. I’m your host, Shalone Cason, and as always, we’ll begin in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
It started in Antioch
Long ago, Jesus’s followers spread the Good News to a big city called Antioch.
“it was in Antioch that the disciples were first called Christians.” (Acts 11:26)
That’s where Christians got their name! Saint Peter and Saint Paul both lived there for a while, and the way Antioch prayed is where our story begins.
Its prayers came from Antioch
An old Catholic encyclopedia tells us where Byzantine worship comes from.
“It is derived from that of Antioch.” (Catholic Encyclopedia, “The Rite of Constantinople”)
It grew from the way Antioch prayed, then grew up in a great city called Constantinople. Its old name was Byzantium, and that’s where the word Byzantine comes from!
One faith, many ways to pray
The Catechism tells us why Catholics pray in different ways.
“Churches of the same geographical and cultural area came to celebrate the mystery of Christ through particular expressions characterized by the culture” (Catechism 1202)
Byzantine and Roman Catholics believe the same things and share the same seven sacraments. We just pray differently: Byzantine churches are full of icons, and the whole Liturgy is sung!
A big Church family
A Byzantine catechism tells us how the Catholic Church is put together.
“It is in these, and formed out of them, that the one and unique Catholic Church exists.” (Christ – Our Pascha 285)
The Catholic Church is a big family of Churches, each with its own bishops. The Latin Church is the biggest. The Ruthenian, Ukrainian and Melkite Churches are Byzantine. Together, they’re one Church!
Together with the Pope
What makes all these Churches Catholic? The same catechism tells us.
“The first among self-governing Churches is the Church of Rome, because its presider is the Pope of Rome, the successor of the apostle Peter.” (Christ – Our Pascha 291)
The Pope takes Saint Peter’s place, and all these Churches are united with him. So Byzantine and Roman Catholics can receive Communion in each other’s churches!

And that’s the Byzantine Rite in a nutshell. It’s a form of prayer started in Antioch, and it is one of the many ways that Catholics can pray while still being one church in communion with the Pope! Thanks for learning with me, and until next time, stay holy, my friend.

lessons.title: What Does Byzantine Mean?
lessons.about: A city named for its founder, an emperor's new capital, and a way of praying that spread across the world, for kids.

quiz.q: Where does the word “Byzantine” come from?
choices: The city of Byzantium, named for Byzas
quiz.why: The city was “naturally called Byzantion” after Byzas, its founder.

quiz.q: “Byzantine” is a way of praying that many different peoples share.
quiz.why: True! Greeks, Slavs, Arabs and others pray the Byzantine liturgy, which spread from Constantinople.

quiz.q: Byzantium was renamed ____, after Emperor Constantine.
quiz.why: Constantine made it his capital, and the city took his name: Constantinople.

quiz.q: What did Byzantine Catholics keep?
choices: Their Byzantine prayers, and unity with Rome
quiz.why: They kept their Byzantine way of praying and stayed in communion with the Church of Rome.

quiz.q: Byzantine Catholics and Orthodox Christians pray the same Byzantine liturgy.
quiz.why: True! The difference is unity with the Pope. The Catechism says our communion “lacks little to attain the fullness” (CCC 838).

transcript: Byzantium, Constantinople, Istanbul...what do these 3 names have in common? Well, these are all names of one city, and the word Byzantine comes from this city. Not only that, but Byzantine Rite Catholics get their traditions from here too. Let’s explore more with this lesson. I’m your host, Shalone Cason, and let’s begin in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
A city named for Byzas
A long time ago, a leader named Byzas founded a city, and it took his name.
“Byzas, after whom the city was naturally called Byzantion” (Catholic Encyclopedia, “Constantinople”)
Byzantion, or Byzantium, was a Greek city on a narrow strait where Europe meets Asia. It was the city of Byzas. So when we say “Byzantine,” we mean “from Byzantium.”
Constantine’s new capital
Emperor Constantine, the first Christian emperor, chose Byzantium for his new capital.
“the solemn inauguration of the new city did not occur until 11 May, 330” (Catholic Encyclopedia, “Constantinople”)

Constantine gave the city a new name: Constantinople, which means the city of Constantine! It was also called a “New Rome.” Its great church was Hagia Sophia, which means Holy Wisdom. So Byzantium became Constantinople.
A way of praying that spread
The way Constantinople prayed spread far beyond the city. The Byzantine Rite was...
“by far the most widely spread in the world.” (Catholic Encyclopedia, “The Rite of Constantinople”)

This means that this way of praying spread all over. Missionaries carried the Gospel from Constantinople to many peoples, like the Slavs in Kyiv. Greeks, Slavs, Arabs, and others all prayed this same way. So “Byzantine” means a way of praying!
Still with the Pope
A Byzantine catechism tells how the Church of Kyiv stayed close to the Church of Rome. Kyiv
“remained in communion with the Church of Rome” (Christ – Our Pascha 307)

Over the years, Rome and Constantinople drifted apart. But the Church of Kyiv kept its Byzantine prayers and stayed united with Rome. Byzantine Catholics get their history and traditions from Constantinople and Kyiv.
Close to the Orthodox
The Catechism says Catholics and the Orthodox are very close. The Orthodox community...
“lacks little to attain the fullness” (Catechism 838)

This means that it wouldn’t take much for our churches, Catholic and Orthodox, to reunite. That’s because Orthodox Christians pray the same Byzantine liturgy, with the same icons and feasts. The difference is unity with the Pope. Even though we are so close, it will be hard for everyone to agree, soWe pray that one day we’ll all be together again!

So what does Byzantine mean? It was the name of a city that became Constantinople, the capital of the Roman Empire. It also became the name of the way people from that city prayed, and even though Orthodox and eastern catholics both share the Byzantine tradition, only the Eastern Catholics are in full communion with the Pope. Thanks for learning with us, and until next time, stay holy my friend

lessons.title: Inside a Byzantine Church
lessons.about: A wall of icons, doors that open to heaven, and Communion from a golden spoon: a look inside a Byzantine church, for kids.

quiz.q: What is the wall of icons called?
quiz.why: The iconostasis is a wall of icons that separates and unites the sanctuary and the nave.

quiz.q: In an icon of Mary, she points us to Jesus.
quiz.why: True! The Mother of God holds Christ and points to him, showing us the way.

quiz.q: The doors in the middle of the iconostasis are called the ____ Doors.
quiz.why: The Royal (or Holy) Doors are in the center of the iconostasis.

quiz.q: How do Byzantine Catholics receive Holy Communion?
choices: From a cup they hold themselves
quiz.why: The priest gives the Body and Blood of Christ with a spoon, for the cleansing from sins.

quiz.q: The Church holds all lawfully recognized rites to be of equal right and dignity.
quiz.why: True! Catechism 1203: all lawful rites are “of equal right and dignity.”

quiz.q: Match each one to what it is.
quiz.why: Byzantine churches have a wall of icons called an iconostasis, with the Royal Doors in the middle, and Communion is given with a golden spoon.

transcript: What does it look like inside Byzantine Churches? Do they look just like Roman Cathothic churches and why do they take communion with a spoon? Let’s find out with today’s lesson. I’m your host Shalone Cason, and let’s begin in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
A wall of icons
The first thing you notice is a wall of icons in front of the altar. It is a wall that...
“separates and at the same time unites the sanctuary and nave.” (Christ – Our Pascha 600)
The wall is called the iconostasis. The altar side is like heaven, and the side where the people stand is like our world. The icons look at us from heaven, so it is more like a window than a wall.
The doors to the Kingdom
A great Ukrainian archbishop said...
“the doors to God’s eternal kingdom.” (Christ – Our Pascha 601)

In the middle of the wall are the Royal Doors. When they open during the Divine Liturgy, it shows that God opens heaven to us. The priest comes out through them to bring us the Gospel and Holy Communion.
Icons point to Christ
Every icon points to one person, as the Catechism explains.
“principally represents Christ.” (Catechism 1159)
On one side of the Royal Doors is the icon of Christ, blessing us. On the other is Mary, the Mother of God, holding Jesus and pointing to him. Mary always shows us the way to her Son!
Communion with a spoon
Byzantine Catholics receive Holy Communion from a golden spoon. The priest gives...
“the most pure Body and precious Blood of Christ for the cleansing from sins.” (Christ – Our Pascha 646)
Long ago, an angel touched the prophet Isaiah’s lips with a burning coal, and his sin was taken away. In the same way, Jesus comes to our lips in Holy Communion to make us clean.
Different, but equal
The Church says every lawful way of praying is...
“of equal right and dignity” (Catechism 1203)
A Roman Catholic church looks different inside, but it teaches the same faith. Both come from the apostles. Together they show us more of Jesus than either one could alone!

In a nutshell, Byzantine Churches have a wall of icons called an iconostasis, with royal or Holy doors in the middle. They take communion with a spoon, and the differences between Eastern and Western catholic churches reveal other ways we can worship Christ. Thanks for learning with us. I’ve been your host, Shalone, and until next time, stay holy, my friends.

lessons.title: The Sign of the Cross
lessons.about: Why Byzantine Catholics make the Sign of the Cross from the right shoulder to the left, and what the three fingers mean, for kids.

quiz.q: Why do we make the Sign of the Cross?
quiz.why: Christ – Our Pascha 626: the Christian “professes faith in the Most Holy Trinity.”

quiz.q: Which shoulder do Byzantine Catholics touch first?
quiz.why: Christ – Our Pascha 626: “from the right shoulder to the left.”

quiz.q: Three fingers joined stand for the Holy ____.
quiz.why: Christ – Our Pascha 626: joining the first three fingers is “a sign of our profession of faith in the Holy Trinity.”

quiz.q: The Church holds all lawfully recognized rites to be of equal right and dignity.
quiz.why: True! Catechism 1203: all lawful rites are “of equal right and dignity.”

quiz.q: Put the Byzantine Sign of the Cross in order.
quiz.why: Christ – Our Pascha 626: “from the forehead to the breast and from the right shoulder to the left.”

transcript: Did you know Byzantine Catholics make the sign of the cross from right to left? Which shoulder do you touch first? They also use their hand to teach themselves about the Trinity. Want to know more? Well, look no further. I’m your host Shalone Cason, and let’s begin in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
A prayer with your whole body
The Byzantine catechism says what the Sign of the Cross is.
“the Christian professes faith in the Most Holy Trinity” (Christ – Our Pascha 626)
When we make the Sign of the Cross, we say who God is: Father, Son and Holy Spirit. It is a prayer we say with our words and with our hands.
Right shoulder first
The catechism tells us where the hand goes.
“from the forehead to the breast and from the right shoulder to the left” (Christ – Our Pascha 626)
Byzantine Catholics touch their forehead, then their chest, then the right shoulder, then the left. We trace the cross of Jesus, who died and rose for us!
Three fingers
The catechism explains the fingers.
“Joining the first three fingers of our hand is a sign of our profession of faith in the Holy Trinity” (Christ – Our Pascha 626)
Three fingers together are for the Trinity. The last two fingers bend down to the palm, for Jesus: he is God and also truly human.
Different, but equal
Roman Catholics go left to right. The Church says every lawful way of praying is...
“of equal right and dignity” (Catechism 1203)
Roman Catholics touch the left shoulder first. Neither way is wrong. It is the same cross and the same God, and the Church loves both ways.

And that was the sign of the cross, in the Byzantine Rite, in a nutshell. It is a prayer that uses your whole body. You touch your right shoulder first and use three fingers to represent the Trinity. Thanks for learning with us. I’ve been your host, Shalone, and until next time, stay holy, my friends.

lessons.title: What Is Infallibility?
lessons.about: What it means that the Pope is infallible, and what it doesn't mean, for kids.

quiz.q: What job did Jesus give Peter?
quiz.why: Luke 22:32: “you must strengthen your brothers.”

quiz.q: Infallibility means the Pope always knows who will win the big game.
quiz.why: False! Catechism 891: the gift is for “a doctrine pertaining to faith or morals.”

quiz.q: Infallible means can't be ____.
quiz.why: Infallible means unable to be wrong. Catechism 889: Jesus gave his Church “a share in his own infallibility.”

quiz.q: The Pope never makes any mistakes at all.
quiz.why: False! The Catholic Encyclopedia says infallibility “is not attributed to every doctrinal act of the pope.”

transcript: We all make mistakes, but can our church’s leader, the Pope, ever be wrong? Let’s learn more in this lesson. I’m your host Shalone Cason, and let’s begin in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
A gift from Jesus
The Catechism says Jesus gave his Church
“a share in his own infallibility.” (Catechism 889)
Infallible means “can’t be wrong.” Jesus is the Truth. He shares this gift with his whole Church, so that what he taught the apostles is kept safe for us.
Jesus prayed for Peter
Jesus told Saint Peter,
“you must strengthen your brothers.” (Luke 22:32)
Jesus prayed that Peter’s faith would not fail. Then he gave Peter a job: help the other apostles stay strong. The Pope does that same job for the Church today.
About faith and being good
The Pope’s special gift is for teaching
“a doctrine pertaining to faith or morals” (Catechism 891)
Faith is what we believe about God. Morals are how God wants us to live. The gift isn’t for math homework, the weather, or who wins the big game!
Not everything he says
A Catholic book says infallibility
“is not attributed to every doctrinal act of the pope” (Catholic Encyclopedia, Infallibility)
The Pope is a person like us. He can make mistakes, and he goes to confession too. Only his rare, solemn teaching for the whole Church is infallible.

So can the Pope ever be wrong? Yes, if he’s predicting the weather or answering a math problem. But he can’t be wrong if he teaches on Faith or Morals. Thanks for learning with us. I’ve been your host, Shalone, and until next time, stay holy, my friends.
